assertions.text: Output contains at least one markdown table (using | column | syntax)
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Weekday Hours | Overtime Threshold (Policy) | Hourly Rate | Weekday Pay? |

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Pay?', 'Rate?')
assertions.evidence: Weekday Pay?, Premium Pay?, Weekly Pay?, Result? column headers

assertions.text: Scenario names describe work patterns or conditions ('Part-time weekday', 'Full week with overtime', 'Sunday shift') — not outcomes ('Gets overtime', 'Double pay').
assertions.evidence: 'Just under the threshold', 'At the threshold', 'Just over the threshold', 'Positive rate'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Weekday hours', 'Sunday hours', 'Hourly rate', 'Weekly pay?') — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: Columns: Weekday Hours, Sunday Hours, Holiday Hours, Hourly Rate, Weekday Pay?

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Weekday Hours | Overtime Threshold (Policy) | Hourly Rate | Weekday Pay? |

assertions.text: The overtime threshold boundary (40 hours) is covered with at least a value at the threshold and one above.
assertions.evidence: 'At the threshold | 40 | 40 | 20 | 800' and 'Just over the threshold | 41 | 40 | 20 | 830'

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Table 1: Weekday Regular and Overtime Pay ... Table 2: Sunday and Holiday Premium Pay ... Table 3 ... Table 4

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 has 5 rows, Table 2 has 4 rows, Table 3 has 3 rows, Table 4 has 3 rows

assertions.text: Payable hours categorisation (1x regular, 1.5x overtime, 2x Sunday/holiday) and pay calculation (hours × rate) are in separate tables
assertions.evidence: Table 1 embeds formula '830 = 40×20 + 1×20×1.5' directly in pay column, mixing classification and calculation rather than separating rate-selection from arithmetic verification.
